top_stories.title: Microsoft Authenticator Flaw Let Permissionless Android Apps Steal Work Account Tokens
top_stories.summary: Microsoft has patched CVE-2026-80097, a vulnerability in Microsoft Authenticator for Android that allowed a permissionless malicious app to impersonate trusted Microsoft applications like Teams and steal work account sign-in tokens. The fix is included in Authenticator for Android version 6.2606.4246, and users are advised to update immediately.

top_stories.title: Microsoft urges Entra ID admins to migrate users to passkeys
top_stories.summary: Microsoft is urging Entra ID administrators to migrate users from SMS and voice authentication to phishing-resistant methods such as passkeys. Microsoft has set a February 2027 deadline for the retirement of SMS and voice authentication in Entra ID, after which continued use of these methods will cause sign-in disruptions.

top_stories.title: Cisco Rethinks Privileged Infrastructure Access
top_stories.summary: Cisco has launched Privileged Infrastructure Access, a solution designed to replace standing administrative access with identity-bound, cryptographic controls. The product targets privileged access management for critical infrastructure, competing in the PAM space by eliminating persistent admin credentials.

top_stories.title: Passkey enrollment and account recovery, the new weak point
top_stories.summary: This article addresses passkey enrollment and account recovery vulnerabilities in Microsoft Entra ID, focusing on weak points that can undermine passkey security. It covers specific mechanisms including Registration campaigns, Temporary Access Pass, and protecting security-info registration as part of a multi-part series on migrating from MFA to passkeys.

top_stories.title: Microsoft 365 Token-Replay Attacks Compromise 97 Accounts at 79 Organizations
top_stories.summary: Researchers disclosed an adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) campaign targeting Microsoft 365 that captured and replayed authentication tokens to compromise 97 accounts across 79 organizations. The attack bypasses MFA by stealing session tokens post-authentication rather than credentials, undermining standard identity security controls.

news.title: Stolen staff logins are spreading attacks between K-12 school districts
news.summary: MS-ISAC reported that 808 of its 6,116 K-12 member organizations had staff credentials circulating on dark web marketplaces during the last school year. Attackers are using stolen staff logins to phish within districts and then pivot laterally to other connected districts.

news.title: Even after PHP2Shell, blast radius matters more than a CVSS score
news.summary: Token Security published analysis arguing that limiting access for service accounts, API keys, and AI agents is critical to reducing breach impact, using the PHP2Shell vulnerability as a case study. The piece focuses on the principle of least privilege and blast radius reduction as complementary to vulnerability patching in modern IAM and secrets management practices.

news.title: American Organizations Under Attack: Skyw4lker Device Code Phishing Campaign Exposed
news.summary: A phishing campaign dubbed Skyw4lker has been identified targeting U.S. organizations using device code phishing techniques that abuse legitimate cloud authentication mechanisms. The attack method bypasses traditional credential theft by exploiting OAuth device code flows to gain unauthorized access to corporate accounts.

news.title: ShinyHunters-Exploited Oracle PeopleSoft Zero-Day Turns Out to Be Three Chained Flaws
news.summary: A critical Oracle PeopleSoft vulnerability exploited by ShinyHunters consists of three chained flaws—an SSRF, an internal management interface exposure, and a third component—patched together under CVE-2026-35273 in June. PeopleSoft is an enterprise platform used for HR and identity-related workflows, and the exploit chain has been actively used since May.

news.title: Microsoft releases Windows OOB updates to distrust eMudhra certificates
news.summary: Microsoft released out-of-band Windows updates to revoke trust in certificates linked to compromised eMudhra certificate authority keys. The updates target systems that do not receive automatic certificate trust updates, addressing a PKI trust chain compromise affecting a recognized CA.

news.title: GoAhead TLS Flaws Allow Revoked Client Certificates and Enable Session Decryption
news.summary: A security flaw in the GoAhead embedded web server's TLS implementation failed to enforce certificate revocation checking, allowing revoked client certificates to successfully authenticate against affected systems. The vulnerability affects builds using the OpenSSL backend with mutual-TLS configurations where a certificate revocation list (CRL) is configured but never actually applied during the authentication process.

news.title: AI-Generated Fake Login Pages Are Making Account Takeovers Easier
news.summary: AI-generated fake login pages are enabling more sophisticated account takeover attacks by allowing attackers to more easily recreate convincing login screens impersonating trusted brands. These pages can capture both passwords and MFA codes, or hijack authenticated sessions, effectively bypassing multi-factor authentication protections.

news.title: Dell expands cyber recovery tools to protect identity
news.summary: Dell Technologies is expanding its cyber recovery tools to include protection and restoration of identity systems, not just data. The move addresses scenarios where identity infrastructure controlling access is compromised during a cyberattack, adding identity resilience as a component of its recovery portfolio.

news.title: AI Agents Are Creating a New Layer of Cybersecurity Spending
news.summary: Akamai launched a security product designed to protect AI agents, joining Okta, Palo Alto, Cisco, CrowdStrike, and Zscaler in the emerging AI agent security market. The article covers the growing cybersecurity spending category around AI agents, which act autonomously and require new identity and access controls.

news.title: Dell extends cyber resilience to identity, AI environments and quantum-safe storage
news.summary: Dell Technologies has extended its cyber resilience portfolio to include identity systems, with PowerProtect software capable of restoring compromised identity platforms to a clean, trusted state after an attack. The identity protection capability is one of three focus areas in the new release, alongside AI environments and quantum-safe storage.

news.title: Keeper Security、2026年版Gartner(R) 「特権アクセス管理のマジック・クアドラント(TM)」に2年連続で選出
news.summary: Keeper Security has been named in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Privileged Access Management for the second consecutive year. The announcement was made by Keeper Security APAC K.K., the company's Asia-Pacific division.

news.title: AI agent security with policy-driven access control
news.summary: A new article examines security approaches for AI agent deployments, focusing on policy-driven access control as a solution to visibility and governance gaps. Research from the Cloud Security Alliance indicates 70% of organizations have AI components in production while 82% lack real-time visibility into AI runtime behavior, with only 21% having adequate controls in place.

news.title: Akeyless Recognized in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Privileged Access Management
news.summary: Akeyless has been recognized in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Privileged Access Management. The inclusion coincides with Akeyless expanding its Runtime Identity Security platform to cover human privileged access, in addition to AI agents and machine identities.

news.title: Xage Security Named in 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Privileged Access Management
news.summary: Xage Security has been named in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Privileged Access Management, recognized for its Ability to Execute and Completeness of Vision. Xage focuses on identity-based Zero Trust solutions for high-stakes operational environments.

news.title: Who Authorized That Agent? Enforcing AI Authority Before the Action
news.summary: The article addresses the challenge of authorization and access control for AI agents, arguing that security policies must be enforced at runtime before agents execute actions. The piece focuses on how traditional IAM and authorization frameworks need to adapt to govern AI agent behavior, touching on concepts of authority enforcement relevant to access management professionals.

news.title: Trust Is Not What It Seems — and Fraudsters Are Counting on It
news.summary: Threat actors are bypassing technical security controls by using AI-assisted social engineering to manipulate help desks into granting unauthorized access. The attack vector targets identity verification and authentication processes at service desks, a critical weak point in access management workflows.

news.title: AI Agents as Insider Threats: Inside Microsoft's Bet on a Unified Security Stack
news.summary: Microsoft's Project Perception introduces Guardian Agents designed to monitor and contain anomalous AI agent behavior within its security stack. The initiative raises questions about identity and authorization controls for AI agents, which increasingly require the same access governance considerations as human or non-human identities.

news.title: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 1,000 Security Holes
news.summary: Microsoft released a record-breaking patch batch addressing at least 974 security vulnerabilities across Windows and other software. AI is being credited with accelerating vulnerability discovery, though security experts note organizations are struggling to keep pace with testing and deploying the volume of fixes.
